newsitem.title: USA: Stocks jump as Wall Street toasts Fed no rate hike decision.
newsitem.headline: Stocks jump as Wall Street toasts Fed no rate hike decision.

text.p: Stocks ended sharply higher on Tuesday, as the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged added more spark to the market's fiery recovery from last Friday's plunge.

Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 114.74 points, or 1.47 percent, at 7,918.10 after storming 109 points higher on Monday on the back of Friday's 247-point loss.
The Nasdaq composite index jumped 31.19 points, or nearly 2 percent, at 1,600.71 on the strength of technology stocks.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 20-8 on heavy volume of 547 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Fed left key interest rates unchanged amid clear signs that the economy is growing at a moderate pace with low inflation.

"The Fed did nothing today, and my guess is that they're not going to do anything probably through the end of the year," said Lawrence Chimerine, managing director at the Economic Strategy Institute, a Washington-based think tank.

The central bank last tightened policy on March 25, when it raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, a move that sparked a sell-off of nearly 10 percent in the blue-chip Dow index. The Fed has since held the line on interest rates.
"We were able to bounce back with the Fed's non-action, the UPS settlement and there was a lot of money flowing into technology stocks," said one trader.

The stock surge masked some stormy volatility. The Dow had earlier scored gains of more than 100 points but whipsawed lower in the minutes following the Fed's announcement, losing 75 points, before heading sharply higher again.
Technology stocks dominated the gains as some money managers, looking for more growth and cheaper valuations, rotated money out of blue chips and into that sector, analysts said.

Among the big movers, Gillette Co., which tumbled Friday and Monday it guided analysts' estimates lower, recouped lost ground as Merrill Lynch raised its rating on the stock. It ended up 2-3/4 to 85-3/4 on the NYSE.
